name: Medial parapatellar approach to the distal femur
aliases: medial knee arthrotomy for distal femur
region: anterior medial knee and distal femur
corridor: Medial retinacular and capsular arthrotomy with lateral patellar dislocation and optional quadriceps extension

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with the knee freely flexed and the patella mobile enough for controlled lateral displacement.

setup.text: Prepare the entire limb, plan incision length from fracture morphology, and preserve options for proximal quadriceps extension and fluoroscopic retrograde-nail access.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the patella, patellar tendon, tibial tubercle, medial joint line, medial epicondyle, and course of the long saphenous vein.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal slightly oblique medial parapatellar incision from about 5 cm above the superior patellar pole toward the tibial tubercle without raising broad skin flaps.

superficial_interval.text: Preserve skin perfusion and the long saphenous vein where possible; expect small infrapatellar saphenous branches near the medial and inferior patella.

deep_interval.text: Incise the medial patellar retinaculum and capsule, lengthen proximally into quadriceps if needed, and dislocate the patella laterally with controlled knee flexion.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with saphenous branches, medial retinaculum, joint capsule and synovium, then distal femoral articular surface.

structures_encountered.text: Medial retinaculum, capsule, patella, patellar tendon, quadriceps tendon, trochlea, femoral condyles, menisci, and cruciate region are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Infrapatellar saphenous branches, long saphenous vein, patellar tendon insertion, skin blood supply, menisci, and articular cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid broad skin flaps and forceful lateral patellar dislocation; inadequate release can avulse the patellar tendon from the tibial tubercle.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the extensor mechanism gently and distribute pressure away from patellar cartilage; lengthen the arthrotomy rather than levering against the tendon.

exposure.text: Provides wide anterior visualization of both femoral condyles and the articular surface for reconstruction and retrograde-nail entry.

limitations.text: Posterior Hoffa fragments may not be adequately visualized, and the approach does not provide the same direct medial extra-articular or vascular corridor as the adductor-magnus approach.

extensions.text: Extend proximally into quadriceps for broader distal-femur exposure or distally toward the tibial tubercle for additional joint access.

indications.text: Use for medial femoral-condylar and selected intra-articular distal-femur fractures, and as an access option for retrograde nailing.

relative_contraindications.text: Use a fragment-specific medial or posterior exposure when a posterior coronal fragment cannot be reduced safely through the anterior arthrotomy, and avoid compromised medial skin when another route is available.

implant_implications.text: Allows direct articular reduction and central retrograde-nail starting-point assessment; protect cartilage and verify that screws or nail components remain extra-articular.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, notch, and condylar oblique views as appropriate to confirm articular congruity, retrograde entry, alignment, and implant containment.

closure.text: Repair capsule and medial retinaculum anatomically, close any quadriceps extension with heavy absorbable suture, then close subcutaneous tissue and skin without strangulating medial flaps.

complications.text: Complications include saphenous sensory disturbance or neuroma, patellar-tendon avulsion, wound compromise, extensor weakness, stiffness, infection, and articular malreduction.

bailouts.text: If lateral patellar displacement remains unsafe, extend the retinacular or quadriceps release; add a fragment-specific approach rather than accepting an unseen posterior reduction.

procedure_applications.condition: A medial condylar or intra-articular distal femur fracture needs broad anterior articular visualization
Retrograde nailing of an intra-articular distal extension requires medial parapatellar joint entry

questions.question: Which sensory nerve branches are encountered medially?
questions.answer: Infrapatellar branches of the saphenous nerve.

questions.question: Why should broad skin flaps be avoided?
How is exposure increased proximally?
questions.answer: By extending the arthrotomy into the quadriceps tendon.
